content:
Sam Patel: Hi team — trying to redeem promo code REDEEM-2026-XY during checkout, dashboard shows it active for our org but API returns `{ \"error\": \"invalid_or_expired\" }`. Can someone check?
Sam Patel: curl I used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/promos/claim
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"code":"REDEEM-2026-XY","org_id":"org_5543","email":"sam@acme.com"}'
```
Sam Patel: Response: HTTP 400, body: `{\"error\":\"invalid_or_expired\", \"reason\":\"constraint_mismatch\"}`
Jordan (Support): Thanks Sam — can you drop the org_id and the time you tried? I'll repro.
Sam Patel: org_id org_5543, tried at 2026-03-17T15:11:03Z. Also screenshot of dashboard (shows code active): https://files.redwood.ai/screenshot/ab12
Jordan (Support): Reproduced locally hitting claim endpoint with same payload — getting 400 + `{\"error\":\"invalid_or_expired\",\"meta\":{\"missing_constraints\":[\"org_tier\"]}}`.
Jordan (Support): Dashboard UI shows promo active because the admin view doesn't surface validation constraints during listing. Escalating to eng. @maeve can you take a look?
Maeve (Eng): Looking now — can you provide the promo id from the dashboard (hover over code or share link)?
Jordan (Support): Promo id from dashboard: promo_7890.
Maeve (Eng): Thanks. Quick summary of what I'm seeing: promo_7890 has an explicit claim-constraint set at creation: `org_tier:startup`. The claim service enforces that constraint by checking org metadata `org_tier` on the org record. For orgs created via the SSO/migration flow we recently shipped, the `org_tier` field wasn't backfilled, so it's missing. When constraints exist and the org metadata is missing, the validator returns constraint_mismatch which surfaces as invalid_or_expired.
Maeve (Eng): TL;DR: promo is active, but server-side constraint validation rejects the claim because the org is missing a metadata key. UI shows active because it relies on promo state, not per-org constraint checks.
Jordan (Support): Got it — helpful. Is this an easy fix or do we need a backfill?
Maeve (Eng): Short term: we can (a) manually grant a promo credit to the user/org, or (b) patch claim-service to treat missing metadata as "no match" in a safer way for this specific constraint type. Long term: we should run a backfill to populate `org_tier` for migrated orgs and add a rule in the dashboard to display constraints.
Asha (Billing): I can apply a manual credit now if you want. Sam — confirm you want the credit applied to org_5543 and I will note it as a temporary mitigation.
Sam Patel: Yes please, apply to org_5543. Appreciate it.
Asha (Billing): Manual credit applied: grant_id grant_2026_434, amount $100 promo credit. Trans ID: trx_998877. You should see it on the org billing page within a minute.
Sam Patel: I see the credit, thanks!
Maeve (Eng): I'll open a remediation ticket: 1) backfill org metadata for orgs migrated since 2025-11, 2) add dashboard indicator for constrainted promos, 3) add a small claim-service patch to return a clearer error message when constraint keys are missing.
Maeve (Eng): For tracking: ENG-6421 opened, assigning to infra/etl for backfill.
Jordan (Support): Thanks @maeve and @asha. Sam — leaving this thread open but marking as mitigated since you have the manual credit. Please ping if anything else. :thumbsup:
PromoBot: Incident created: ENG-6421 - promo constraint backfill (priority: P3)
Sam Patel: All good, thanks everyone!
